title: Fluid column anchoring and density profiles for hybrid table views
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Our current virtualized table controls and density modes feel disjointed for mixed-content pages (lists with cards, tables with attachments). Column resize, pinning and density toggles operate independently which causes jarring layout shifts when users switch contexts (e.g., from compact to roomy). Engineers report edge-case bugs where cached row heights invalidate virtualization heuristics during density toggles, and PMs have collected multiple support threads from customers about losing column context after pinned columns collapse on narrow viewports.

Goal: Deliver a cohesive design pattern that: (1) introduces a fluid column anchoring metaphor that prevents context loss during density changes and multi-column resizes; (2) defines a small set of density profiles (Compact, Balanced, Spacious) driven by tokens and clear heuristics; (3) documents animation and layout rules for virtualization to avoid reflow thrash; (4) provides accessible keyboard-first affordances for resize & density switching.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Fluid column anchoring: when a user resizes or pins a column, capture an "anchor delta" relative to the viewport and apply an easing-preserved transform during density transitions so the anchored column remains in view rather than snapping. This is a UI-level transform layered on top of the virtualization layer (non-destructive).
- Density profiles: expose three canonical profiles implemented via token sets (spacing, rowHeight, font-size-scale, internal padding). Each profile has a deterministic mapping to virtualization rowHeight hints to avoid mid-transition measurement invalidation.
- Hybrid view rules: for pages that mix cards and tables, define a composition rule that treats table containers as independent measurement zones; density switches for the page should include an optional per-zone confirmation to avoid unintended collapses.
- Resize affordances: introduce a two-step resize interaction for long touch/trackpad drags — a 'preview rail' that shows a ghost width while dragging and only applies the final width after mouseup (helps virtualization and reduces reflow). Keyboard +/- modifiers should adjust by 8px tokens with announced values via ARIA live.
- Sorting/filtering parity: ensure density/profile changes preserve sort state and keep active filter chips pinned above the table; when density compaction hides filter text, show chip count with tooltip.

Design artifacts and links:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/Table-Density-Profiles-Design?node-id=412%3A0
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Table+Density+Profiles+PRD
- Prototype (Cypress visual test plan): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/xxxx

Acceptance notes: anchor transform must be interruptible (user can scroll or reflow should cancel the transform); virtualization must receive stable rowHeight hints before commit; keyboard resize must announce new width and new column order if reflow triggers collapse.

Open questions for engineering: how to expose 'rowHeightHint' API across runtime variants (hosted vs dedicated vs private) so platform autoscaling/batching heuristics can remain compatible with UI-prescribed hints. Also need guidance from infra on whether a ghost preview rail can be done purely client-side without additional measurement rpcs that risk rate-limiting.
acceptance_criteria: Three density profiles implemented in component tokens and selectable from Console toggles.
Anchored column remains visible during density change in 90% of tested breakpoints (visual regression tests).
No virtualization layout thrash observed in automated test harness (rowHeight hints stable after density switch).
Keyboard resize and density switch pass accessibility audit (screen reader announces relevant changes).
Design spec and dev handoff documented with example PR and Storybook stories.
comments: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting with PM (Lara Cho) and Eng (Ravi Patel) — aligned on three density profiles and anchoring goal.
2025-02-24: Early Figma mocks uploaded — requested simplified 'ghost rail' prototype to validate perception of stability during density change.

2025-02-27: Usability study (n=6) with power users — participants preferred anchored transitions, but 2/6 found transition timing too slow; lowered easing time from 300ms to 200ms as follow-up iteration.
2025-03-02: Eng review — flagged potential issue where virtualization uses lazy measurement; Eng proposed adding stable 'rowHeightHint' prop and a debounce window to coalesce rapid density toggles.
2025-03-04: Updated spec with keyboard ARIA announcements and added Storybook knobs. Assigned dev spike to ENG-21022 to implement rowHeightHint API (2-week spike).
